newsitem.title: UGANDA: Museveni to deploy 3,000 troops against rebels in west.
newsitem.headline: Museveni to deploy 3,000 troops against rebels in west.

text.p: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni will send some extra 3,000 troops to the war-torn western region to curb Moslem-based rebels of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), state radio said on Thursday.

The radio quoted Museveni, speaking at a rally in the western town of Kasese, as saying the troops will be deployed in areas likely to be infiltrated by the rebels Uganda says are backed by neighbouring Sudan.
"More arrangements have already been made to ensure that rebels are flushed out," Museveni said without elaborating.
Museveni, himself a former guerrilla leader, ruled out talks with the ADF rebels whose leadership remains a mystery. The rebels operate mainly from Ruwenzori mountains.
"Those rebels who will surrender can be pardoned, while those who want to be captured will be charged with treason," the radio reported.
Early this month, the ADF entered and took temporary control of the western town of Bundibugyo in fierce clashes that left scores of people dead and displaced more than 700,000.
On Tuesday, a U.N. official said more than 10,000 of the Ugandans who had fled the fighting have returned in the last few days to Uganda from the northeast of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
"In the last few days 12,000 to 13,000 Ugandans in the Beni area have returned to Bundibugyo in western Uganda," U.N. World Food Programme spokeswoman Brenda Barton said in Nairobi.
She said about 15,000 Ugandans still remained in the Congolese town of Beni.
Despite seizing power after a five-year bush war in 1986, Museveni has faced numerous rebellions in the north and western parts of the east African country.
